# losforgos: LineageOS apps for GrapheneOS

Builds the user-space LineageOS apps from upstream with GitHub Actions, signs them with one
stable key, and publishes them as GitHub releases that [Obtainium](https://github.com/ImranR98/Obtainium)
can track. Every app is installed as an ordinary app under the id `org.losforgos.<name>`;
nothing here is a system app.

## Install and update with Obtainium

Releases are per app and per variant. Add one Obtainium entry per app with:

- Source URL: this repository
- Filter release titles by regex: `^Glimpse ` (the app's title, plus a space)
- Filter APKs by regex: `-unmodified\.apk$`
- Fallback to older releases: on

`obtainium-apps.json` has these entries ready to import. I could not test the import
format against a device yet, so treat that file as best effort and check the first import.

Verify a download: the APK's signing certificate SHA-256 is in the repository variable
`CERT_SHA256` and in every release's attestation (`gh attestation verify <apk> --repo OWNER/REPO`).

## Dialer notes

The Dialer is installed as `org.losforgos.dialer`, so it can sit next to a system Dialer. Set it as
the default phone app (Settings, Apps, Default apps, Phone app) to use it.

- Works: calls, Recents, contact matching, the in-call notification with Hang up, Speaker and Mute.
- No visual voicemail and no call recording; both need system privileges.
- Phone numbers match contacts whichever way the country prefix is written, using the SIM's region.
  A number with an explicit different prefix does not match.
- The search box and smart dial are not covered by prefix matching yet.
- The live-update chip for ongoing calls needs Android 16.
- Settings, Sounds and vibration needs "Modify system settings"; the app opens that page for you.

## How it works

- `apps.toml` pins one upstream commit per app. The `bump upstream` workflow opens a pull
  request on the 1st and 15th of each month when upstream moved.
- `build` fetches the pinned commit, renames the application id, sets a monotonic version
  (`versionCode = YYYYMMDDNN`), applies patches for modified variants, and builds an unsigned
  release APK. This job has no access to secrets.
- `release` (only on `main`, in the `release` environment) signs the APKs, attests them, and
  creates one release per app: tag `<app>-v<version>`, assets `<app>-<version>-<variant>.apk`
  plus a `.sha256`. An app is only released again when its build inputs changed.
- Native libraries and 16 KB alignment are listed in each build log. Memory tagging has to be
  tested on a device; CI cannot do it.

## Obtainium links

The badge, the per-app links, `docs/obtainium.html` and `obtainium-apps.json` are generated from
`apps.toml`. After changing the app list, run `python3 scripts/losforgos.py deeplink --write`;
the `plan` job of the build workflow fails when they are out of date (`deeplink --check`).
The badge opens `docs/obtainium.html` through GitHub Pages (Settings, Pages, deploy from branch
`main`, folder `/docs`), because Obtainium's public redirect page only accepts a single app and
GitHub strips `obtainium://` links from this file.

## One-time setup

On your Mac (Linux works too), in a clone of this repository:

```sh
git pull
scripts/setup-signing.sh
```

It creates the signing key (openssl only, no Java), installs and logs in the GitHub CLI if
needed, creates the `release` environment limited to `main`, stores the signing secrets and the
`CERT_SHA256` variable, and allows Actions to open pull requests. Then back up
`~/.losforgos-keystore` and its password; if they are lost, every installed app has to be
uninstalled before an update signed by a new key will install.

Publish the first releases:

```sh
gh workflow run build.yml --ref main -f release=true -f force=true
```
